params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# --- recency weighting (deterministic structure, no model judgement) --------
# How many of the newest turns travel VERBATIM into the prompt. Everything
# before them phases out to a bounded preview -- more from the last turns,
# phase-out before, hard facts kept (R-OS-3 handover).
RECENT_TURNS = int("${SUMMARIZER_RECENT_TURNS:-12}")
# Per-turn character cap on the phased-out older turns.
PHASEOUT_CHARS = int("${SUMMARIZER_PHASEOUT_CHARS:-200}")
# Per-item character cap on tool call/result previews in the context section.
TOOL_CHARS = int("${SUMMARIZER_TOOL_CHARS:-200}")
# How many tool-activity lines enter at most, newest kept.
ROUND_LINES = int("${SUMMARIZER_ROUND_LINES:-40}")

# The prompt lives HERE, in the glue phase -- an llm cell has no params.system
# slot (P15 lesson); its system state arrives by message, and this hive sends
# it fresh with every batch (accumulate-replace per path, so re-sending is an
# idempotent upsert).
INSTRUCTIONS = (
    "You are the session summarizer of an agent. A conversation generation "
    "has closed; write the handover summary its successor wakes up with, so "
    "the transition is not noticeable.\n"
    "Weight by recency: the recent turns deserve the most detail, older "
    "turns fade to their essentials. Always keep hard facts - names, dates, "
    "numbers, decisions, preferences, open tasks - even from the oldest "
    "turns.\n"
    "Write plain prose, no headings. Do not address the user; describe the "
    "session. An empty or short session yields a short, honest summary - "
    "never invent content the session does not contain.")

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
session = str(hop.get("session_id", "") or ctx.get("session_id", "") or "default")


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def role_of(t):
    return "user" if t.get("origin") == "user" else "assistant"


if lane == "in_batch":
    # The collector's close batch (R-OS-6): messages[] the whole day in order,
    # the raw round rows in the top-level slot `rounds`. One batch, one prompt.
    msgs = [m for m in d.get("messages", []) if isinstance(m, dict)]
    recent = msgs[-RECENT_TURNS:] if RECENT_TURNS > 0 else []
    older = msgs[:len(msgs) - len(recent)]
    lines = ["Session %s closed with %d turns." % (session, len(msgs)), ""]
    if older:
        lines.append("## %d older turns (condensed to %d chars each, oldest first)"
                     % (len(older), PHASEOUT_CHARS))
        for t in older:
            lines.append("- %s: %s" % (role_of(t),
                                       str(t.get("text", "") or "")[:PHASEOUT_CHARS]))
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("## Recent turns (verbatim, oldest first)")
    if recent:
        for t in recent:
            lines.append("- %s: %s" % (role_of(t), str(t.get("text", "") or "")))
    else:
        lines.append("(none - the session had no turns)")
    # Tool rounds as context. The leg-* rows are the collector's bookkeeping
    # (assembly legs, eviction reports) and carry no session content of their
    # own -- the turns above already are the conversation.
    tool_lines = []
    for r in d.get("rounds", []) or []:
        if not isinstance(r, dict) or r.get("role") not in ("assistant", "tool"):
            continue
        t = r.get("turn")
        items = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([t] if isinstance(t, dict) else [])
        for x in items:
            if not isinstance(x, dict):
                continue
            kind = x.get("type")
            if kind not in ("tool_call", "tool_result"):
                continue
            word = "call" if kind == "tool_call" else "result"
            tool_lines.append("- iter %s %s %s: %s"
                              % (r.get("iter", 0), word, x.get("id", ""),
                                 str(x.get("text", "") or "")[:TOOL_CHARS]))
    if tool_lines:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("## Tool activity (capped previews, newest last)")
        lines.extend(tool_lines[-ROUND_LINES:])
    emit([{"header": {"route": "llm", "session_id": session,
                      "turn_count": str(len(msgs))},
           "system": {"instructions": {"text": INSTRUCTIONS}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text",
                         "text": "\n".join(lines)}]}])

if lane == "in_answer":
    text = ""
    for m in d.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("origin") == "assistant" and m.get("type") in ("text", None):
            text = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    if not text.strip():
        # system.* is accumulate-replace per path: an empty update would
        # REPLACE a real handover with nothing. Rather no update, loud lane.
        emit([{"header": {"route": "summary_error", "session_id": session,
                          "error_code": "empty_summary"},
               "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                             "text": "summary failed for session %s: "
                                     "empty_summary (the writer returned no "
                                     "text)" % session}]}])
    # ONE emission, and its body IS the update: the `system.handover` upsert
    # an llm cell consumes without a provider call. No messages[] -- messages
    # would trigger an inference at the receiver.
    emit([{"header": {"route": "summary", "session_id": session,
                      "summary_chars": str(len(text))},
           "system": {"handover": {"text": text}}}])

if lane == "in_error":
    # Degradation (GH #100 ruling): a failed call leaves on its own route
    # instead of being swallowed -- the parent tree decides (drain or alarm).
    # No retry here: retry is edge business, not template business.
    code = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "") or "unknown_error"
    emit([{"header": {"route": "summary_error", "session_id": session,
                      "error_code": code},
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "summary failed for session %s: %s"
                                 % (session, code)}]}])

# Terminal by design: an unknown lane parks, it does not guess.
emit([])

recent_turns.description: How many of the newest turns of the closed session travel VERBATIM into the summarizer prompt (SUMMARIZER_RECENT_TURNS). Everything before them phases out.

phaseout_chars.description: Per-turn character cap on the phased-out older turns (SUMMARIZER_PHASEOUT_CHARS). A bounded preview, counted in the prompt, never silently gone.

tool_chars.description: Per-item character cap on tool call/result previews in the prompt's tool-activity section (SUMMARIZER_TOOL_CHARS).

round_lines.description: How many tool-activity lines enter the prompt at most (SUMMARIZER_ROUND_LINES); the newest are kept.

description.purpose: The glue half of the summarizer: shapes a closed session's write batch into ONE recency-weighted prompt for the writer llm (recent turns verbatim, older turns condensed and counted, tool rounds as capped context), and forms the writer's answer into ONE system.handover update - the fresh memory the next generation wakes up with. The prompt lives here, in the glue phase, because an llm cell has no params.system slot; the instructions ride as a system update next to the prompt document.
description.use_when: Inside the summarizer hive, behind the collector's write batch. The parent edge names the entry lane (hop.route == 'write' -> set_hop 'in_batch').
description.not_in_scope: No inference (the writer llm answers). No judgement about what the day was worth - the weighting is deterministic structure, the judgement is the model's prose. No retry on failure: retry is edge business; a failed call leaves on summary_error and the parent tree decides. Not the writer of any system path outside its own two: system.instructions on the lane INTO ./writer (re-sent with every batch, accumulate-replace) and system.handover on the way out. R-OS-1 says one writer per slot; it does not say one slot per writer.
description.emits_meaning: route llm: the summarizer prompt for the writer - system.instructions the shipped prompt, messages[] one user document, hop.session_id and hop.turn_count for the internal edge to promote. route summary: ONE emission per batch whose body is nothing but {system: {handover: {text}}} - the update an llm cell consumes without a provider call; hop.session_id and hop.summary_chars say whose and how long. route summary_error: the degradation lane - a failed or empty summary, hop.error_code the cause, one assistant text naming session and cause. An unknown lane emits nothing (empty multi-send, terminal by design).
description.consumes_meaning: Three lanes, named by hop.route: in_batch (the collector's close batch - messages[] the whole day, top-level slot rounds the raw round rows, hop.session_id/turn_count/round_count the sizes), in_answer (the writer's finished summary, session in context), in_error (the writer's error message, hop.error_code rides through). The session is read from hop.session_id first, context.session_id second.
examples: close batch of 40 turns -> older 28 condensed to 200 chars each and counted, newest 12 verbatim, tool rounds as capped previews -> one prompt on route llm
writer answers 'the user configured helix...' -> one emission on route summary with system.handover.text and summary_chars
provider 500 -> the writer's error arrives on in_error -> one emission on route summary_error with error_code provider_error
empty session -> the prompt says '0 turns' and the instructions demand a short honest summary instead of invention
